From 76903b2057c8677c2c006e87fede15f496555dc0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Daniele Ceraolo Spurio <daniele.ceraolospurio@intel.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 08:37:22 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] drm/xe/pxp: Clear restart flag in pxp_start after jumping
 back

If we don't clear the flag we'll keep jumping back at the beginning of
the function once we reach the end.

Fixes: ccd3c6820a90 ("drm/xe/pxp: Decouple queue addition from PXP start")
Signed-off-by: Daniele Ceraolo Spurio <daniele.ceraolospurio@intel.com>
Cc: Julia Filipchuk <julia.filipchuk@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Julia Filipchuk <julia.filipchuk@intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260324153718.3155504-9-daniele.ceraolospurio@intel.com
(cherry picked from commit 0850ec7bb2459602351639dccf7a68a03c9d1ee0)
Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Vivi <rodrigo.vivi@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pxp.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pxp.c
index fa82d606953e..088a1ab75f70 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pxp.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pxp.c
@@ -512,7 +512,7 @@ static int __exec_queue_add(struct xe_pxp *pxp, struct xe_exec_queue *q)
 static int pxp_start(struct xe_pxp *pxp, u8 type)
 {
 	int ret = 0;
-	bool restart = false;
+	bool restart;
 
 	if (!xe_pxp_is_enabled(pxp))
 		return -ENODEV;
@@ -541,6 +541,8 @@ static int pxp_start(struct xe_pxp *pxp, u8 type)
 					 msecs_to_jiffies(PXP_ACTIVATION_TIMEOUT_MS)))
 		return -ETIMEDOUT;
 
+	restart = false;
+
 	mutex_lock(&pxp->mutex);
 
 	/* If PXP is not already active, turn it on */
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in the `pxp_start` function within `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pxp.c`, where a `restart` flag was not cleared after a jump back, causing an infinite loop.

**Modifications in each file:**
- **`drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pxp.c`** (function `pxp_start`):
  - Removed the initializer `= false` from the declaration of the `restart` variable (line 512).
  - Added an explicit assignment `restart = false;` after the timeout check (before the mutex_lock) to ensure the flag is reset upon re-entering the critical section.

**Relationship between modifications:**
The move of the `restart` reset from the variable declaration to a later point in the function ensures that any previous iteration that set `restart` to `true` (e.g., via a jump back to the beginning of the function) does not persist that value. Without this change, the flag remained `true`, causing a continuous loop where the function restarted indefinitely upon reaching its end. The fix correctly resets the flag right before the mutex-locked region that handles PXP activation, breaking the cycle.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
bool restart = false;
restart = true;  // one of the assignments inside the switch
if (restart) goto wait_for_idle;
```
Reason:
The `restart` flag is initialized to `false` at function entry, but when the function jumps back to `wait_for_idle:` via `goto wait_for_idle;`, the flag retains its previous `true` value (set earlier in the same iteration). Since there is no reset of `restart` after the label, the flag remains `true` on re-entry, causing the function to loop infinitely by always taking the `goto wait_for_idle` at the end.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
bool restart;
restart = false;  // inserted after the wait_for_idle label and before the mutex_lock
```
Reason:
By moving the declaration to `bool restart;` (without initialization) and explicitly setting `restart = false` after the jump-back label (`wait_for_idle:`), the flag is cleared at the start of each new iteration. This ensures that `restart` is only set to `true` when a specific condition during that iteration warrants a rerun, thereby breaking the infinite loop.
